title: Rust: Rc, Arc, and RefCell
description: Use Rc, Arc, and RefCell for shared ownership and interior mutability.

steps.title: Rc (Reference Counting)
steps.description: Create an `Rc<String>` from `"Hello"`. Clone it and verify both point to the same allocation. Print the reference count and the value.

verification.failureMessage: Create Rc, clone it, print value and reference count.

steps.title: RefCell (Interior Mutability)
steps.description: Create a `RefCell<i32>` with value 0. Borrow mutably to increment to 10. Borrow immutably to print the value. Then try to cause a runtime borrow panic (and catch it).

verification.failureMessage: Set RefCell to 10 and print it.

steps.title: Rc<RefCell<T>> for Shared Mutable State
steps.description: Create an `Rc<RefCell<i32>>`. Share it between multiple owner scopes. Each scope modifies the value. Print the final value.
hints: Clone the Rc for each scope.

verification.failureMessage: Share a mutable counter across multiple owners and print final value.

steps.title: Arc for Thread Safety
steps.description: Create an `Arc<Mutex<i32>>` and share it across 5 threads. Each thread increments the value. Print the final value after all threads finish.

verification.failureMessage: 5 threads increment a shared counter, print 5.

steps.title: Graph with Rc
steps.description: Create a simple graph using Rc: `struct Node { value: i32, neighbors: Vec<Rc<RefCell<Node>>> }`. Create 3 connected nodes and traverse them, printing each node's value.
hints: Rc enables shared ownership (multiple nodes can reference the same neighbor).
RefCell enables mutability (can add neighbors after creation).

verification.failureMessage: Create a graph node and print its value and neighbor values.
